corrections.license: Public domain (dedication in README: 'All of this is public domain, do whatever you want with it'; no LICENSE file)
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE file (repo holds only README.md, main.cpp, platform.h, rans_byte.h); the README dedicates the code to the public domain, which this catalog treats as copyable; no patent grant. main.cpp (a ryg_rans-style harness timing rANS variants with __rdtsc) contains no FSE code, and the FSE row (325 MB/s encode, 440 MB/s decode) is identical to the Proba80 FSE row in the FiniteStateEntropy README, so it was probably copied rather than measured on the Ryzen 1700 with enwik8; the FSE comparison is doubtful and the standard-rANS comparison is the credible one. No compiler or flags stated; single file, single machine; last commit 2018-04-27.

notes: Numbers match README exactly; derived ratios fine. Confirmed FSE row equals FSE README Proba80 row (Cyan4973/FiniteStateEntropy dev README line 33). Usability changed to copyable per public-domain dedication rule.

tier_reason: README shows test.cpp output on book1 (577.1-619.1 MiB/s decode, Core i7 1065G7) next to separately run FSE (370.3 MB/s decode) and ryg_rans SIMD (512.8-565.6) outputs; CMakeLists sets -O3 -msse4.1, but the compiler for the headline run is not named and the baselines are not in the repo's harness, so first-party C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMakeLists.txt sets -O3 -msse4.1; README says tested with clang v10 and gcc v9.3.0 on Linux and clang/MSVC 2019/2022 on Windows, but does not name the compiler for the Ice Lake run (FSE run says 'same compiler' with a Windows path; ryg_rans run was Linux clang)
corrections.caveats: Single file (book1), single machine, first-party. Baselines (FSE demo, ryg_rans exam_simd_sse41) were run as separate programs, ryg_rans under Linux/clang while the range coder's compiler is not named. Units differ: the range coder reports MiB/s, ryg_rans labels MiB/s-computed values as MB/s, FSE reports MB/s. The same README shows FSE Huffman mode (-h) decoding faster at 800.9 MB/s and its own AVX-2 port at 1,373 MiB/s, so the SSE 4.1 coder beats only FSE/tANS (about 1.6x) and ryg_rans SIMD rANS (about 1.1x). Encoder not optimized (51.9 MiB/s vectorized-path encode). Last commit 2023-05-12.

notes: All claimed numbers present on README; Unlicense LICENSE file confirmed, 30 stars, last commit 2023-05-12 (abandoned is correct at >3 years).

tier_reason: README Table 2 numbers match, and compiler (gcc 7.3.0), flags (CMakeLists -O3 -march=native) and CPU (i7-7700) are stated, but the repo's harness (src/intersect.cpp) only times Slicing; the PEF and Roaring runs are not in public benchmark code, so not A. The peer-reviewed DCC 2021 paper (same setup) shows RUP/Slicing 7.6-10.6x faster than PEF on AND queries, which supports B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README Table 2 (microseconds per 2-list intersection) Slicing vs PEF: Census-Income 11.56 vs 115.17, Census-1881 0.18 vs 0.92, Weather 25.70 vs 213.00, Wikileaks 0.47 vs 2.51; about 5x to 10x faster than PEF (derived from page data). Versus Roaring: slower on 3 of 4 (11.56 vs 4.68, 0.18 vs 0.15, 25.70 vs 13.37), faster on Wikileaks (0.47 vs 0.86). DCC 2021 paper Table 2 (ms per AND query, TREC queries): RUP 0.32/1.67/1.78 vs PEF 2.48/12.54/19.72 on Gov2/ClueWeb09/CCNews (about 7.8x/7.5x/11x, derived from page data); Roaring 0.32/1.64/1.29 is equal or faster.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 7.3.0; CMakeLists.txt sets -std=c++14 -O3 -march=native -ggdb (Release default); clang builds add -stdlib=libc++
corrections.caveats: Baseline is PEF (ds2i), not SDSL or sux, so baseline_in_list is false. Slicing loses to Roaring on most README datasets and ties or loses in the DCC 2021 paper, so the win is against cardinality-partitioned succinct/compressed lists (PEF and others) only. The repo's intersect.cpp times only Slicing; competitor timings come from the authors' code (ds2i, CRoaring) run outside this repo. Space is larger than PEF (e.g. 2.23 vs 2.03 bpi on Census-Income; 4.31 vs 3.12 bits/int on Gov2). Old hardware and gcc 7.3; last commit 2023-01-08.

notes: Paper PDF fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com/jermp/jermp.github.io/master/assets/pdf/papers/DCC2021.pdf (Pibiri, DCC 2021, pp. 293-302); it states i7-7700, gcc 7.3.0, -O3 -march=native and uses competitors' own code. Downgrade A to B only because the baseline harness is not public; MIT license, 19 stars confirmed.
